title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court, the All-China Women's Federation, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, and the National Health Commission on Strengthening the Implementation and Enforcement of the Personal Safety Protection Order System
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, All-China Women's Federation, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, Ministry of Justice, National Health Commission

Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Personal Safety Protection Order System

Fa Fa [2022] No. 10

In order to further improve the work of preventing and stopping domestic violence, to protect the legitimate rights and interests of family members, especially women, minors, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, in accordance with law, and to safeguard equal, harmonious, and civilized family relations and to promote family harmony and social stability, the following opinions are hereby put forward regarding strengthening the implementation of the personal safety protection order system:

1. Adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Thoroughly implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law and the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important discourses on focusing on family, family education, and family traditions, actively cultivate and practice core socialist values within the family, cultivate good family traditions, promote family virtues, and maximize the prevention and suppression of domestic violence.

2. Adhere to the principle of protecting victims in accordance with law, in a timely manner, and effectively. All departments shall continuously increase their efforts to assist victims of domestic violence in areas such as temporary shelter, legal aid, and judicial relief, and establish a multi-level, diverse, and three-dimensional rescue system. They shall deeply understand the private and sudden nature of domestic violence, raise the awareness of victims of domestic violence regarding evidence, and guide them to preserve and submit evidence in a timely manner in accordance with law.

3. Adhere to the principle of respecting the true will of the victim. When handling complaints, reports, or requests for help related to domestic violence, as well as when accepting cases or conducting referral and placement work, all departments shall solicit the opinions of victims regarding what safety protection measures to take, whether to apply for a personal safety protection order, and the handling of the perpetrator, and shall increase psychological counseling for victims.

4. Adhere to the principle of protecting the privacy of the parties. When accepting cases, assisting in enforcement, or fulfilling mandatory reporting obligations, all departments shall pay attention to protecting the privacy of the parties, especially minors. If the victim has already moved out of the shared residence with the perpetrator, the whereabouts or contact information of the victim shall not be disclosed to the perpetrator, and the current residence of the victim shall not be listed in relevant documents or receipts. Personal safety protection orders shall generally not be made public.

5. Promote the establishment of a coordinated anti-domestic violence working mechanism among all departments. Actively promote the inclusion of domestic violence prevention and control in the comprehensive social security management system, and utilize the evaluation mechanism for peace-building assessments. Improve the anti-domestic violence work system involving the joint participation of people's courts, public security organs, civil affairs departments, judicial administrative departments, education departments, health departments, and women's federations. Fully leverage the achievements of information technology construction to strengthen data sharing and coordination among departments. Explore the use of special case files, graded early warning, and other methods to accurately track and conduct real-time supervision.

6. Public security organs shall strengthen their concepts and awareness of intervening in domestic violence in accordance with law, increase their efforts in handling domestic violence police reports, strengthen admonitions to perpetrators, and issue domestic violence admonition letters in accordance with laws and regulations. They shall focus on collecting and preserving evidence, actively cooperate with people's courts in collecting evidence ex officio, and provide police dispatch records, admonition letters, and inquiry (interrogation) records. Where conditions permit, they may establish a domestic violence police report linkage mechanism and an admonition notification mechanism with people's courts, civil affairs departments, and women's federations.

7. Civil affairs departments shall strengthen training and guidance for residents' committees, villagers' committees, social work service institutions, relief management institutions, welfare institutions, and the like. Residents' committees, villagers' committees, social work service institutions, relief management institutions, welfare institutions, and their staff, upon discovering that a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct is suffering or is suspected of suffering domestic violence, shall promptly report to the public security organs. Implement the "Guiding Opinions on Doing a Good Job of Shelter and Relief for Victims of Domestic Violence," strengthen the construction of temporary shelter facilities, allocation of personnel and funds, and provide victims of domestic violence with timely referral and placement, legal aid, marriage and family dispute mediation, and other relief services.

8. Judicial administrative departments shall increase legal aid efforts for victims of domestic violence, smooth the application channels for legal aid, and improve the service network. Local authorities may, based on actual circumstances, rely on local women's federations and the like to establish legal aid workstations or contact points to facilitate victims of domestic violence seeking legal aid nearby. Strengthen the publicity of laws and regulations such as the Anti-Domestic Violence Law, the Law on the Protection of Minors, the Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests, and the Law on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly. Fully leverage the advantages of people's mediation, do a solid job in investigating and resolving marital and family disputes, and prevent the occurrence of domestic violence.

9. Medical institutions, in the course of diagnosis and treatment, upon discovering injured persons who may have suffered domestic violence, shall carefully record the injured person's information and diagnosis and treatment records, and accurately, objectively, and comprehensively record the injured person's chief complaint, injuries, and treatment process in the medical records. Establish a medical-police linkage mechanism. If, during diagnosis and treatment, it is discovered that a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct is suffering or is suspected of suffering domestic violence, the medical institution shall promptly report to the public security organs and actively cooperate with the public security organs in collecting medical diagnosis and treatment materials.

10. Schools and kindergartens shall strengthen the publicity and education of laws and regulations such as the Law on the Protection of Minors, the Law on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency, and the Anti-Domestic Violence Law. Focus on the coordination of home-school and home-kindergarten cooperation. If it is discovered that a minor is suffering or is suspected of suffering domestic violence, they shall, in accordance with the "Regulations on School Protection of Minors," promptly report to the relevant departments such as public security, civil affairs, and education. Pay attention to protecting the privacy of minors and strengthen psychological counseling and intervention efforts.

11. People's courts shall establish a "green channel" for accepting personal safety protection order cases, increase the intensity of ex officio evidence collection, and issue personal safety protection orders in a timely manner in accordance with law. Each basic people's court and its dispatched people's tribunals shall provide guidance services in the case filing hall or litigation service center for parties applying for personal safety protection orders.

12. Adhere to the principle of the best interests of the minor. When various departments hear the opinions of minors on the facts of domestic violence or prepare interrogation records, they shall fully consider the physical and mental characteristics of minors, provide appropriate venue environments, adopt questioning methods that minors can understand, and protect their privacy and safety. When necessary, a psychological counselor or social worker may be arranged to assist in the work. In cases involving personal safety protection orders where a minor is the victim, the people's court may notify a legal aid institution to provide legal aid to the minor. If a minor child provides testimony as a witness, they may not appear in court to testify.

13. When various departments handle complaints, reports, requests for help related to domestic violence, or handle marital and family disputes, if they discover that a party is suffering or faces an imminent risk of domestic violence, they shall proactively inform the party that they may apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection order.

14. After issuing a personal safety protection order, the people's court shall serve it on the parties within 24 hours, and at the same time serve it on the local police station, residents' committee, and villagers' committee. It may also, depending on the circumstances, serve it on the local women's federation, school, organization for the protection of minors, federation of persons with disabilities, and lawfully established organization for the elderly, etc.

15. When serving a personal safety protection order, the people's court shall focus on interpretation and persuasion education, urge the respondent to comply with the personal safety protection order, and inform them of the legal consequences of violating the personal safety protection order. If the respondent fails to perform or violates the personal safety protection order, the applicant may apply to the people's court for compulsory enforcement. If the respondent violates the personal safety protection order and does not constitute a crime, the people's court shall give an admonishment, and may, depending on the severity of the circumstances, impose a fine of not more than 1,000 yuan or detention for not more than 15 days.

16. When serving a personal safety protection order, the people's court may simultaneously serve a notice of assistance in enforcement on the local police station, residents' committee, villagers' committee, women's federation, school, etc. The notice of assistance in enforcement shall clearly specify the matters for which assistance is required. The relevant entities shall provide assistance in accordance with the contents of the notice of assistance in enforcement.

17. During the validity period of a personal safety protection order, the content of assistance in enforcement by public security organs may include: assisting in supervising the respondent's compliance with the personal safety protection order; if, during the validity period of the personal safety protection order, the respondent violates the personal safety protection order, the public security organ, upon receiving the report, shall promptly dispatch police to stop the illegal act; upon receiving the report, provide rescue and protection to the victim, and collect and preserve evidence; if it is discovered that the respondent violates the personal safety protection order, notify the people's court, etc.

18. During the validity period of a personal safety protection order, the content of assistance in enforcement by residents' committees, villagers' committees, women's federations, schools, etc., may include: conducting regular follow-up visits and tracking records during the validity period of the personal safety protection order, filling out follow-up visit forms or record sheets, which shall be signed by the parties upon expiration and then fed back to the people's court; if it is discovered that the respondent violates the personal safety protection order, they shall criticize and educate the respondent, fill out a situation feedback form, and help the victim contact the people's court or public security organ in a timely manner; conduct rule-of-law education for the perpetrator, and when necessary, provide psychological counseling to the perpetrator and the victim, etc.

19. When various departments handle complaints, reports, requests for help related to domestic violence, or handle marital and family disputes, they may explore the introduction of social work and psychological counseling mechanisms to alleviate the psychological trauma of victims and minor children, correct the perpetrator's cognitive and behavioral deviations, avoid the escalation of violence, and fundamentally reduce the occurrence of serious incidents.

20. All departments shall fully recognize the importance of the personal safety protection order system, increase learning and training efforts, become familiar with the specific content such as the subjects who may apply for a personal safety protection order, the issuance procedure, and the specific content of assistance in enforcement, and strengthen the popularization and promotion of the personal safety protection order system.

March 3, 2022
